_what: Every closed list (z.enum / z.literal / z.nativeEnum) an agent tool's input accepts, keyed by file and declaring line, with why the set is the agent's own vocabulary rather than a name it must guess (AI-1l). Enforced by tests/sop/tool-input-constraints.test.ts: a new list fails until reasoned here; a removed one fails until its row goes.

constraints.src/features/ai/server/actionDescriptors: HTTP verbs, the agent's own vocabulary. GET is left out on purpose: this is the ERP WRITE tool, and reads have their own.
The ERP ownership rule's two modes in our own model (a product attribute, or whole websites); a third mode would be a new feature, not a different name.
Commerce configuration scopes this tool writes: default, or the project's own website. Commerce's own words for them; store-view scope is deliberately not offered.
The setup checklist's own three step states, defined by this extension; the tool's description says what each means.
Discriminator of assign_erp_products' selection: a brand as buyers see it. Our own shape.
Discriminator of assign_erp_products' selection: chooses which field the selection carries (a category id). Our own shape, documented beside each branch.
Discriminator of assign_erp_products' selection: the start of the SKUs. Our own shape.
Discriminator of assign_erp_products' selection: a list of SKUs. Our own shape.
constraints.src/features/ai/server/dataInstallerDesc: Demo Builder's own two datapack stores, as for save_datapack_zip's source: the Data Installer service's catalog and the team's datapack library. The description says which is the default and when the library needs the demo-builder engine.
Demo Builder's own two datapack stores: the Data Installer service's catalog and the team's datapack library. Not a name the agent must guess; the description says which is the default.
Demo Builder's own two datapack stores: the Data Installer service's catalog and the team's datapack library. Not a name the agent must guess; the description says which is the default.
constraints.src/features/ai/server/lifecycleTools.ts: Which of the current project's own URLs to open; arbitrary URLs are refused by design (the tool takes over the screen). The description lists every target with what it opens.
constraints.src/features/ai/server/readDescriptors.t: The data installer's own four operations for process-datapack (import, export, delete, validate). The service names them so; there is no other spelling an agent could reach for.
constraints.src/features/ai/server/viewTools.ts: vie: Demo Builder's own screens (VIEW_COMMANDS). The set IS the screens that exist; a name outside it opens nothing, and the description lists them.
constraints.src/features/ai/server/dataInstallerDesc: Demo Builder's own two datapack stores, as for start_datapack_import's source: preview_datapack_changes reads the pack's rows from the Data Installer service's catalog or the team's datapack library, and save_store_changes_to_pack reads the installed version's own rows from it (datapack-engine step 05); verify_datapack_install reads the pack it checks the store against from it (2026-11-06). Not a name the agent must guess; the description says what omitting it does.

reset_datapack's answer to the changes it names: Demo Builder's own two choices, keep (save them to the demo's own pack first) or drop (lose them). The refusal that asks spells out both, so nothing is guessed.
constraints.src/features/ai/server/deleteProjectTool: delete_project's answer about the user's changes in a datapack that is not theirs, with removeData: Demo Builder's own two choices, keep (save them as a new datapack named by saveAs) or drop (lose them, in the user's own pack too, as the window's Without Saving does), as reset_datapack's. The CHANGES_NEED_ANSWER refusal spells out both. Written over several lines until 2026-11-13, which this scan reads line by line and so never saw.
constraints.src/features/ai/server/dataInstallerDesc: clear_demo_data's answer about the user's changes in the datapack it uninstalls first (datapack-simplification step-06 C3, 2026-11-13): the same two choices as reset_project's and delete_project's, keep (saved into the user's own pack, or as a new datapack named by saveAs) or drop (lost, in the user's own pack too, as the window's Clear Without Saving does). Read by changesAnswer, described by changesDescriptionFor, in datapackAnswerArgs; the CHANGES_NEED_ANSWER refusal spells out both.
reset_project's answer about the user's changes in the datapack its removeData uninstalls (step-05 S7, owner 2026-11-13): the same two choices as delete_project's, keep (save them as a new datapack named by saveAs) or drop (lose them, in the user's own pack too); both tools read their description from CHANGES_DESCRIPTION. The CHANGES_NEED_ANSWER refusal spells out both.
constraints.src/features/ai/server/dataInstallerDesc: clear_commerce_instance's answers about each project's changes, by project path (datapack-simplification step-06 C6, 2026-11-13): the same two choices as clear_demo_data's, reset_project's and delete_project's, keep (saved as a new datapack named by that path's saveAs) or drop (lost, in the user's own pack too). Read by instanceClearRequest through changesAnswer in datapackAnswerArgs; the CHANGES_NEED_ANSWER refusal names the project and spells out both.

clear_commerce_instance's "I understand" (datapack-simplification step-06 C6, 2026-11-13): the Clear Commerce Instance window's box, which the handler also requires (clear-commerce-instance refuses without understood:true). Only true means anything; a call without it is a validation error the agent corrects by asking the user.
